verdicts.evidence: The stream is now fed. Sent three messages from the composer in one session ('w1verify stream one 3311', 'two 3312', 'three 3313'): three .turn nodes appeared in [data-testid=barn-activity-stream], oldest first, each with a 'You . <relative time>' meta line, and the empty state was replaced on the first send. So it does grow. It does not alternate: no assistant turn is ever appended, and the panel says so in its own words between the turns ('The assistant's replies are in the terminal. Its output is a character stream, not typed events, so this view cannot yet show them as steps with durations.'). Cross-checked in the pod with tmux capture-pane: the prompts were submitted and claude answered, so the replies exist and are simply not parsed into the stream. Turns are also per-session only: reloading /barn/editor put the stream back to 'Nothing sent in this session yet'.
verdicts.defect: Only the user half of the conversation is rendered. AssistantPanel records a turn for each composer send but never produces an assistant turn, so the stream is a list of your own messages rather than the alternating transcript the design draws. Nothing scrolls yet either - with three turns the stream's scrollHeight equalled its clientHeight, so the keep-newest-visible behaviour is untested and unexercised.

verdicts.evidence: Rancher's header is back on /barn/editor (header[data-testid=header] computes to display:flex, height 55px, and [data-testid=header__brand-img] measures 200x36 and renders the SUSE chameleon plus the 'SUSE Rancher Prime' wordmark). The rail's Home entry (a[href=/dashboard/home]) is the working substitute.

Half of it works. verdicts.evidence: Seeded barn.publish.failure with a ten-line log and loaded /barn/extensions/base/build-failed. The card reads: headline 'The publish did not finish: the extension did not build', then the sub-heading 'The line that looks like the problem', then the raw log line 'ERROR in ./pages/Home.vue', then 'Picked out of the log by pattern, not by understanding it - the assistant does not yet read a build log and explain it. Treat this as a pointer to where to look.' No plain-language headline about what went wrong, no sub-line separating build success from the real fault, no explanatory paragraph.
verdicts.defect: Unchanged. What the screen shows is still a regex-picked log line, with a disclaimer saying so. The 'explained' half of the screen is not delivered; the honest labelling is the right call while that is true, and the two genuinely new controls on this screen (the raw-output disclosure and 'Show me <file> at line N') are the useful parts of the answer instead.

verdicts.evidence: The handoff query is live and a publish really happens. Two observations. (1) The query is read and consumed: loading /barn/editor?publish=w1bogus left the URL as /barn/editor with the key stripped and no publish started, while a control key (/barn/editor?w1keep=1) survived untouched - so the stripping is specific to publish/brief. The shipped bundle (barn-0.5.22.umd.min.863.js) shows why: mounted() calls handleHandoff(), which reads $route.query.publish, $router.replace()s the query without publish and brief, and then calls publishTo(e) for 'local' or 'github'. (2) I drove it once, deliberately, to settle the rest: clicked 'Try the publish again' on the build-failed screen. It navigated to /barn/editor/base, stripped the key, and the publish ran to completion - the publish-status strip ended on 'base 0.1.0 installed' and kubectl showed a new UIPlugin, cattle-ui-plugin-system/base, plugin base v0.1.0. I removed that UIPlugin afterwards to put the environment back. Caveat worth recording: screen 08 has no .studio-masthead at all, so the control is the 'Try the publish again' button in the Ways back column rather than a masthead Publish.
